summary: Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Trinity College, Cambridge, and a DCL from Durham University. He held posts at Bramham College, the India Office Library, and the University of London.
Samuel Johnson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge, and Pembroke College, Oxford.

Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Wells Williams worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute from around 1831 to 1832 and later held a post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She held positions at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University in 1991 and also held an academic post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and completed her MA supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under supervisor Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995). He also held a post as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College (attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and Semtokha Rigney School. He served as a teacher at Semtokha Rigney School and as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

Sangharakshita worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Jianmin Chen, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sangye Khadro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi, including St. Stephen's College and the Delhi School of Economics. He has held chairs and posts at the University of Oxford, EHESS, UCLA, and the Collège de France.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under M. K. Ganguli and received traditional training under A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Jadavpur, Utrecht University, and the University of Oxford.

Sanki Ichikawa was a linguistics scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University from 1906 to 1909. He later held academic posts at Tokyo Imperial University (1916–1946) and the Institute for Research in Language Teaching (~1923).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Nārada. He held posts at the University of Rangoon, the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Sara Frumento is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar attested in 2026 as studying for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD, 2002), she has held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.
